title: Chocolate yoghurt cake

ingredients.note: 1 yoghurt pot; the pot is the measuring cup

steps: Stir yoghurt, sugar, flour, baking soda and cocoa with a wooden spoon for 2 minutes until smooth. Fold in the dried fruit.
For a white version, swap the cocoa for grated lemon zest.
Pour into a buttered tin and bake at 180 °C for about 45 minutes, until it pulls away from the sides.
Warm the milk, cocoa, sugar and butter for the glaze. Pour it over the cake once the cake has cooled.
notes: Original measures everything with the yoghurt pot. For the smallest tin, use small pots and only half a teaspoon of soda.

title: Ladyfinger cake

ingredients.note: yolks for the cream, whites for the meringue

steps: Lay everything out. Dip each ladyfinger in milk with a splash of rum (no sugar) and line the first layer.
Beat the softened butter with the yolks, sugar and finely chopped lemon zest into a cream. Spread over the layer.
Sprinkle with a little croquant. Repeat up to 4 layers.
Whip the egg whites to stiff peaks, spread over the top and sides in flames, and bake at 100 °C for 5 to 10 minutes just to set them.
notes: Improvise between layers: dried fruit, thin banana or kiwi slices.

title: Pitka (festive bread)

ingredients.note: white in the dough, yolk to brush

steps: Knead the dough and let it rise for 25 minutes.
Roll it out on the table, spread with beaten egg and crumbled cheese, roll up and cut into triangles.
Arrange in the tin, let rise somewhere warm, brush with the yolk.
Bake at 220 °C for 45 to 50 minutes.
notes: The original lists no yeast, but the dough rises. Check with mum before trusting this one.

title: Chocolate walnut pie
steps: Beat the yolks with half the icing sugar until pale. Add 150 g walnuts and the chocolate melted with the cocoa.
Whip the whites with the rest of the sugar and fold in. Sift in the flour slowly.
Bake in a buttered tin at 170 °C for 35 to 40 minutes.
Once cool, pour over chocolate and sprinkle the remaining walnuts.
notes: The wine appears in the list but not in the method. Mum's secret, presumably.

title: Soda mekitsi
steps: Mix the yoghurt with the soda and salt, add the egg, then add flour little by little until it becomes a dough.
With oiled hands, stretch pieces of dough one by one on foil.
Fry in hot oil until golden.

title: Kozunak (sweet Easter bread)
steps: Make a soft dough. Let it rise twice.
Bake at 180 °C for 50 minutes.
Too much dough? Make small rolls, or a roll with raisins, walnuts, sugar, cinnamon and thick jam.
notes: This is the small batch. The doc also has a double batch (4 eggs, 1.3 kg flour). "Improvise, you can do it."

title: Festive pogacha Eva
steps: Dissolve yeast and sugar in 100 ml of the milk. Add eggs (keep one yolk), salt, vinegar, lard and the rest of the milk.
Add the sifted flour bit by bit until the dough leaves the bowl. Knead and let rise for about an hour.
Divide into 8 pieces, roll each to 3 to 5 mm and brush with melted butter. Stack 4 and roll up; repeat. Cut the rolls into triangles.
Arrange the ends in the centre of a 28 cm tin and the triangles around them. Rise 30 to 40 minutes, brush with yolk and milk, sprinkle seeds.
Bake in a preheated oven for 25 to 30 minutes, lowering to 160 °C if needed. Brush with butter and cover with a cloth.

title: Waffles
steps: Mix the dry ingredients in one bowl and the eggs, milk, butter and vanilla in another.
Combine until smooth.
Pour into a preheated waffle iron and cook 1 to 2 minutes.

title: Boston cream doughnuts

ingredients.note: doc says 20 g; the source uses one 7 g packet

steps: Pastry cream: heat milk and sugar, whisk into yolks and cornstarch, cook until thick, finish with butter and vanilla. Chill.
Dough: dissolve yeast in warm milk with sugar, mix with flour, yolks, salt and spices, knead in the butter. Rise until doubled.
Roll out, cut rounds, rise again, then fry until golden. Cool.
Fill with pastry cream and dip in the chocolate glaze.

title: Three-chocolate cake
steps: Blitz the biscuits to crumbs, mix with the melted butter and press into the base of a springform tin.
Dark layer: heat 150 g dark chocolate with 250 ml cream and 50 g sugar. Dissolve 1 sachet of junket powder in 250 ml milk, add, and stir over medium heat until it thickens without boiling.
Pour over the base and let it set for a few minutes.
Repeat with the milk chocolate, then the white chocolate, letting each layer set so they don't mix.
Chill overnight. Decorate simply, with cinnamon or sweets.

title: Pumpkin waffles with cream cheese
steps: Beat cream cheese, brown sugar and cinnamon until fluffy, about 3 minutes.
Preheat the waffle iron.
Whisk egg, sugar, pumpkin, milk and oil. Add the dry ingredients and whisk until smooth.
Cook the waffles and let them cool in a single layer.
Spread filling on half, top with the rest, cut into wedges.

title: Ginger breakfast elixir
originalTitle: Еликсирът за закуска на Есил Дюран
steps: Grate the ginger.
Blend the lemons with the ginger.
Stir in the honey. Keep in a jar in the fridge; take a spoonful in the morning.

title: Macedonian banitsa
steps: Knead a smooth dough from water, egg, oil, vinegar, salt and flour.
Divide into 30 balls, oil them, cover and rest 5 minutes.
Roll each very thin. Stack in two piles of 15, buttering between sheets. Chill at least 2 hours.
Roll one stack to the size of a buttered round tin. Spread cheese mixed with eggs. Cover with the second stack and tuck the edges.
Brush with butter and egg. Bake at 180 °C for 40 to 45 minutes.

title: Salmon Poke Bowl
steps: Thaw the frozen salmon in the fridge for 12 to 24 hours.
Cut the salmon into 2 cm cubes.
Mix soy sauce, honey, sesame oil and 1 tbsp water.
Set aside 2 tbsp of the dressing.
Add sesame seeds and salmon to the rest, mix gently.
Marinate in the fridge for 20 to 30 minutes.
Rinse the rice until the water runs almost clear.
Bring rice and 360 ml water to a boil, covered.
Simmer on lowest heat for 12 minutes, lid on.
Rest covered for 10 minutes.
Warm rice vinegar, sugar and salt until dissolved.
Fold the vinegar mix into the rice and let it cool to lukewarm.
Steam the edamame for 3 to 4 minutes.
Dice the cucumber.
Dice the avocados just before serving.
Divide the rice between 4 bowls.
Add salmon, avocado, cucumber, sprouts, edamame and leaves.
Sprinkle with chia seeds and pepper, drizzle with the reserved dressing.
notes: Freeze the salmon at -15°C for 5 days first (anisakis), or buy it already frozen. Don’t marinate over 1 hour or it turns salty and firm. Time excludes freezing and thawing. Chia seeds optional.

title: Roast salmon with broccoli
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C.
Toss broccoli with oil, garlic and salt on a tray; roast 10 minutes.
Add the salmon, squeeze over lemon, roast 12 minutes more.

title: Pasta with beetroot pesto
steps: Cook the pasta.
Blend beetroot, walnuts, parmesan, garlic, oil and lemon juice into a pesto.
Toss with the pasta and a splash of the cooking water.

title: Red lentils with eggs and spinach
steps: Soften onion and garlic in oil with cumin.
Add lentils, tomatoes and 500 ml water; simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in spinach, make wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook until set.

title: Chickpea Curry
steps: Mix the ground spices (curry powder, ground coriander, cinnamon, nutmeg, turmeric, pepper) in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Toast coriander and cumin seeds for 1 minute until darker.
Add the curry leaves, cover immediately and cook 20 seconds.
Add the onion with a pinch of salt and cook 5 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger and chili, cook 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the ground spices and tomato paste, stir for 90 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and 1 tsp salt, cook 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in chickpeas, coconut milk, water, tahini and sugar.
Bring to a simmer, cover and cook 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Strip the chard stems, roll the leaves and slice thinly.
Add the chard and simmer 4 to 5 minutes until wilted.
Stir in the garam masala.
Off the heat, add lemon juice, coriander and mint.
Season with the remaining salt and rest 5 to 15 minutes.
Serve with rice or naan.
notes: Chickpeas = 2 tins, drained. Curry leaves optional. 1 chili is mild, 3 is spicy. Chard can be swapped for kale or baby spinach (1 to 2 min). No whole spices: use 1.5 tsp ground coriander and 0.5 tsp ground cumin instead.

title: Shopska salad
steps: Chop tomatoes, cucumber, pepper and onion.
Dress with oil, vinegar and salt.
Grate sirene generously over the top and finish with parsley.

title: Tarator (cold yoghurt soup)
steps: Whisk yoghurt with cold water.
Add grated cucumber, crushed garlic, dill and salt.
Serve cold with oil and walnuts on top.

title: Chicken and Potato Traybake
steps: Preheat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan).
Mix the juice of 1 lemon, 1 tbsp oil, 1 tsp oregano, salt and pepper in a bowl.
Coat the chicken thighs in the mixture.
Put potatoes, carrots, onion wedges and garlic in a large roasting tin.
Add the remaining oil, oregano, salt and pepper.
Quarter the second lemon, squeeze over the veg and add the quarters to the tin.
Toss the veg and spread in a single layer.
Lay the chicken on top and roast 20 minutes.
Take the chicken out, stir the veg and spread it out again.
Nestle the chicken in the veg, pour over any juices and roast 20 minutes more.
notes: 8 skin-on thighs. Use new potatoes, halved; carrots whole if small, otherwise batons. Onions in 8 wedges, garlic unpeeled and lightly crushed. Veg must be in one layer or it steams; use 2 tins if needed.

title: Triple Chocolate Layer Cake
steps: Preheat the oven to 175°C.
Grease two 23 cm round cake pans, line with baking paper and grease the paper.
Whisk flour, 64 g cocoa, sugar, baking soda, baking powder, 1 tsp salt and espresso powder in a large bowl.
In another bowl, whisk oil, eggs and 2 tsp vanilla until combined.
Mix in the buttermilk.
Add the dry ingredients and the hot coffee, then whisk until smooth. The batter is thin.
Divide the batter between the pans.
Bake 23 to 26 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool in the pans on a rack for 1 hour.
Loosen the edges, turn out, peel off the paper and cool completely.
For the buttercream, beat the butter on medium speed for 2 minutes until creamy.
Add icing sugar, 64 g cocoa, 3 tbsp cream, 1 tsp vanilla and 1/4 tsp salt.
Beat on low for 30 seconds, then on high for 1 minute.
Adjust texture with more cream if too thick, or more icing sugar or cocoa if too thin.
Level the cake tops with a serrated knife if domed.
Place one layer on a plate and cover the top with frosting.
Add the second layer and frost the top and sides.
Press chocolate chips on top or around the sides.
Chill uncovered for 30 to 60 minutes before slicing.
notes: Use natural cocoa in the cake, not Dutch-process. Split: cocoa 64 g cake / 64 g frosting; vanilla 2 tsp / 1 tsp; salt 1 tsp / 1/4 tsp. Coffee can be hot water; espresso powder and chocolate chips are optional. No buttermilk: 2 tsp vinegar topped up with milk to 240 ml, rest 5 min.

title: Creamy Vegan Mushroom Stroganoff
steps: Wipe the mushrooms clean, then slice or tear them.
Halve the leeks lengthwise, slice, wash in cold water and pat dry.
Heat half the oil in a large deep pan over medium-high heat.
Cook half the leeks and mushrooms 8 to 10 minutes until browned.
Lower to medium, add half the garlic, half the thyme and a pinch of salt, cook 2 to 4 minutes.
Set this batch aside on a plate.
Repeat with the rest of the oil, leeks, mushrooms, garlic, thyme and a pinch of salt, leaving it in the pan.
Whisk stock, soy sauce, Worcestershire and flour until smooth.
Add the wine to the pan, scrape the bottom and simmer 3 minutes.
Whisk in the stock mixture and bring to a simmer.
Add coconut milk, tahini, nutritional yeast, paprika and the remaining salt.
Simmer on medium-low 10 minutes until thick.
Cook the pasta in salted water until al dente and drain.
Stir the mustard into the sauce.
Add pasta and most of the dill, toss to coat.
Serve topped with the reserved mushrooms, remaining dill and pepper.
notes: Use a mix of mushrooms (cremini plus shiitake, oyster or maitake). Don’t wash or salt mushrooms early, or they steam. Worcestershire optional. No wine: deglaze with 60 ml stock.
